text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Lebanon will put on trial the detainees and will not hand over any of them to Japan. The Japanese envoy to Damascus today.
-Lebanon presents evidence to a five-nation monitoring group that Hizbollah has not fired from a civilian-populated area in south Lebanon, killing one Israeli soldier last Friday.
-U.S. Senator Georges Mitchel: The issue of the travel ban on Lebanon will be discussed with the U.S. secretary of state and we will demand that it be lifted.
-The Japanese issue: 48 additional hours before things clear up.
-Israeli gunmen shell the south Lebanon Iqlim al-Toufah mountain ridge and Hizbollah guerrillas wound two South Lebanon Army militiamen in a road side bomb.
-The weekly treasury bill issue of February 27 raised 311.6 billion Lebanese pounds after the Bank of Lebanon restricted sales of most bills.
-Lebanese University teachers to go on a two-day strike over pay demands.
-House Speaker Berri meets his Kuwaiti counterpart in Kuwait.
